parts.title: Ninety Minutes on the Clock
parts.text: Marco, Aisha, and Wren had trained for weeks for the city's junior **culinary** contest, where teams had ninety minutes to cook a three-course dinner. The theme was announced as the clock started: a feast fit for a king. The judges wanted every dish to be **savory**, rich with salt and spice rather than sugar. Marco poured lemon juice, garlic, and herbs over his chicken so it could **marinate** while the others got to work.

parts.title: Heat and Hurry
parts.text: Aisha poured tomatoes and broth into a pot and turned the flame low, letting her soup **simmer** gently. Beside her, Wren pressed and folded her bread dough, working hard to **knead** it smooth. Aisha beat cream and egg yolks with a **whisk** until her sauce turned silky. Suddenly a **pungent** smell of burning garlic drifted across the kitchen. Marco's pan was far too hot, and his sauce began to **scorch**.

parts.title: The Final Plate
parts.text: With ten minutes left, Marco did not panic. He had to **concoct** a new sauce from honey, mustard, and cream, stirring until it shimmered. Then he grated **zest** from a lemon over the chicken, adding a bright, tangy flavor. When the judges cut into the meat, it was **succulent**, tender and full of juice. Wren finished the plate with a sprig of parsley as a **garnish**, and the team stepped back, breathing hard.

parts.title: Taste of Teamwork
parts.text: The trio did not win first place, but the judges praised their courage. Marco learned that a mistake is not the end of a recipe. Aisha and Wren learned that a team can fix almost anything together. They left the kitchen tired, proud, and already planning next year's menu.

definitions.meaning1: To cook gently in liquid just below the boiling point. Example: Let the soup simmer for twenty minutes.
definitions.meaning2: To be filled with a strong feeling that is not yet shown. Example: Anger began to simmer inside him as he waited his turn.
definitions.studentChallenge: Turn the stove down low and let the sauce ___ for an hour.

definitions.meaning1: Salty or spicy in flavor, rather than sweet. Example: Popcorn with butter and salt is my favorite savory snack.
definitions.studentChallenge: Cheese crackers and salted nuts are ___ treats, not sweet ones.

definitions.meaning1: A small decoration added to a dish of food. Example: A single lemon slice was the only garnish on the plate.
definitions.meaning2: To decorate food with a small extra touch. Example: She likes to garnish the soup with fresh herbs.
definitions.studentChallenge: The chef placed a sprig of mint on the cake as a ___.

definitions.meaning1: To make something by mixing different ingredients together. Example: He concocted a smoothie from spinach, mango, and yogurt.
definitions.meaning2: To invent a story or plan. Example: The twins tried to concoct an excuse for being late.
definitions.studentChallenge: With only eggs and flour left, she tried to ___ a dessert.

definitions.meaning1: To burn the surface of something so that it turns brown or black. Example: A hot iron can scorch a shirt if you leave it too long.
definitions.meaning2: To dry up with heat. Example: The summer sun began to scorch the lawn.
definitions.studentChallenge: If the pan gets too hot, the sauce will ___ and taste bitter.

definitions.meaning1: The thin, colorful outer skin of a lemon, orange, or lime, used to add flavor. Example: A pinch of orange zest made the muffins smell wonderful.
definitions.meaning2: Great energy and enthusiasm. Example: She tackled every new project with zest.
definitions.studentChallenge: Grate a little lemon ___ over the cake for a bright, tangy flavor.

definitions.meaning1: Having to do with cooking or kitchens. Example: Her culinary skills include baking bread and making pasta from scratch.
definitions.studentChallenge: The school offers ___ classes for students who dream of running a restaurant.

definitions.meaning1: Having a sharp, strong smell or taste. Example: The pungent smell of raw onions filled the kitchen.
definitions.studentChallenge: The ___ odor of blue cheese lingered in the refrigerator for days.

definitions.meaning1: Full of juice, tender, and delicious. Example: We bit into succulent peaches that were ripe and sweet.
definitions.meaning2: Describing a plant with thick, fleshy leaves that store water. Example: The cactus is a succulent plant that thrives in the desert.
definitions.studentChallenge: The steak was so ___ that juice ran down the plate when the knife went in.

definitions.meaning1: To soak food in a flavorful liquid before cooking it. Example: We marinate the chicken overnight in lemon juice and garlic.
definitions.studentChallenge: Let the tofu soak in soy sauce for an hour so it can ___ before grilling.

definitions.meaning1: To beat or stir quickly, usually to mix ingredients or add air. Example: Whisk the eggs and milk until the mixture is foamy.
definitions.meaning2: A kitchen tool made of looped wires, used for beating. Example: She grabbed a whisk from the drawer to mix the batter.
definitions.studentChallenge: She used a wire ___ to beat the cream until it was thick and fluffy.

definitions.meaning1: To press and fold dough with your hands to make it smooth. Example: Knead the dough for ten minutes before letting it rise.
definitions.meaning2: To rub or squeeze with the hands, as in a massage. Example: The coach began to knead the sore muscle in his leg.
definitions.studentChallenge: Fold and press the dough for ten minutes to ___ it until smooth.
